title: Nelson Mandela is released from prison
summary: Nelson Mandela walked free from Victor Verster Prison after 27 years in custody. He addressed a huge crowd in Cape Town the same day.
reason: President F. W. de Klerk had begun dismantling apartheid under internal unrest, sanctions and economic decline.
significance: It opened the negotiations that ended apartheid in South Africa.
place: Victor Verster Prison, Paarl, South Africa

title: Lithuania declares independence from the Soviet Union
summary: The Supreme Council of Lithuania voted to restore the country's independence, the first Soviet republic to do so.
reason: Gorbachev's reforms allowed the Sajudis movement to win elections on a platform of ending the 1940 Soviet annexation.
significance: It set off the chain of secessions that ended the Soviet Union.
wikipedia: Act of the Re-Establishment of the State of Lithuania

title: Hubble Space Telescope is launched
summary: Space Shuttle Discovery lifted off on mission STS-31 carrying the Hubble Space Telescope, which it released into orbit the next day.
reason: Astronomers wanted a large telescope above the atmosphere, which blurs and absorbs starlight.
significance: Hubble transformed astronomy, from the age of the universe to the study of distant galaxies.
place: Kennedy Space Center, Florida, United States

title: North and South Yemen unite
summary: The Yemen Arab Republic and the People's Democratic Republic of Yemen merged into the Republic of Yemen, with Ali Abdullah Saleh as president.
reason: The weakening of the Soviet Union left the southern socialist state without its patron, and both sides hoped to share newly found oil.
significance: It created a single Yemeni state, though tensions led to civil war in 1994.

title: Iraq invades Kuwait
summary: Iraqi forces crossed into Kuwait and occupied the country within two days. Saddam Hussein later declared it Iraq's nineteenth province.
reason: Iraq was deeply in debt after the war with Iran and accused Kuwait of overproducing oil and slant drilling into Iraqi fields.
significance: It triggered the Gulf War and a long era of US military involvement in the region.

title: Germany is reunified
summary: The German Democratic Republic joined the Federal Republic of Germany, ending 45 years of division. Crowds celebrated at the Reichstag in Berlin.
reason: The fall of the Berlin Wall and the collapse of East Germany's government made unification possible, agreed in the Two Plus Four Treaty.
significance: It made Germany the largest state in the European Community and closed a chapter of the Cold War.

title: Operation Desert Storm begins
summary: A US-led coalition began a massive air campaign against Iraqi forces in Iraq and Kuwait.
reason: Iraq ignored a United Nations deadline of 15 January to withdraw from Kuwait.
significance: It showed the power of precision weapons and led to Kuwait's liberation within weeks.

title: Treaty of Asuncion creates Mercosur
summary: Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay signed a treaty to build a common market in South America.
reason: Newly democratic governments wanted to end old rivalries and open their economies through regional trade.
significance: Mercosur became South America's largest trade bloc.

title: Cyclone strikes Bangladesh, killing about 138,000
summary: A powerful tropical cyclone hit the Chittagong region at night with a storm surge of about six metres.
reason: The low-lying coast of the Bay of Bengal was densely populated and had few cyclone shelters.
significance: It was one of the deadliest cyclones on record and led to a large program of shelters and warnings.

title: Mount Pinatubo erupts in the Philippines
summary: The climactic eruption of Mount Pinatubo on Luzon threw ash and gas into the stratosphere, while a typhoon turned the ash into heavy mud.
reason: The volcano had been dormant for about 500 years before magma rose in early 1991.
significance: Timely evacuations saved thousands, and its aerosols cooled the global climate by about half a degree.
participants: Philippine Institute of Volcanology and Seismology

title: India opens its economy with the 1991 budget
summary: Finance Minister Manmohan Singh presented a budget that cut tariffs, ended much industrial licensing and welcomed foreign investment.
reason: India faced a balance of payments crisis with foreign reserves for only a few weeks of imports.
significance: It began India's economic liberalisation and decades of fast growth.

title: The World Wide Web becomes publicly available
summary: Tim Berners-Lee posted a summary of the World Wide Web project to Usenet, inviting anyone to use it and contribute.
reason: He had built the system at CERN to help physicists share documents across different computers.
significance: The web turned the internet into a mass medium.

title: Hardliners attempt a coup in Moscow
summary: Communist hardliners detained Mikhail Gorbachev and declared a state of emergency, but crowds led by Boris Yeltsin defended the Russian parliament and the coup failed within three days.
reason: The plotters wanted to stop a new union treaty that would hand power to the republics.
significance: Its failure fatally weakened the Communist Party and hastened the end of the Soviet Union.
participants: State Committee on the State of Emergency

title: Linus Torvalds announces Linux
summary: A Finnish student, Linus Torvalds, posted on Usenet that he was writing a free operating system kernel as a hobby.
reason: He wanted a Unix-like system for his new PC and was frustrated by the limits of Minix.
significance: Linux grew into the kernel behind most servers, supercomputers and Android phones.

title: The Soviet Union is dissolved
summary: The Soviet of the Republics formally voted the Soviet Union out of existence, a day after Mikhail Gorbachev resigned and the red flag was lowered over the Kremlin.
reason: Failed reform, economic collapse, nationalist movements and the failed August coup had emptied the union of power.
significance: It ended the Cold War and created fifteen independent states.

title: Maastricht Treaty is signed
summary: Twelve European Community states signed the Treaty on European Union, creating the European Union and a path to a single currency.
reason: After German reunification and the end of the Cold War, leaders wanted deeper integration to anchor Germany in Europe.
significance: It founded the European Union and led to the euro.

title: White South Africans vote to end apartheid
summary: In a whites-only referendum, about 69 percent backed continuing the reform process begun by F. W. de Klerk.
reason: De Klerk called the vote to answer conservative critics and secure a mandate for negotiations with the ANC.
significance: It gave the government a clear mandate to negotiate the end of white minority rule.

title: Alberto Fujimori dissolves Peru's Congress
summary: President Alberto Fujimori, backed by the army, shut down Congress and the courts and suspended the constitution.
reason: He faced a hostile Congress, hyperinflation and the Shining Path insurgency, and claimed democracy was blocking reform.
significance: It began a decade of authoritarian rule in Peru.

title: Los Angeles riots break out
summary: After a jury acquitted four police officers of beating Rodney King, rioting spread across Los Angeles for six days, leaving 63 dead.
reason: The beating had been filmed, and the verdict fed long-standing anger over police brutality and racial inequality.
significance: It became a lasting reference point in American debates on race and policing.

title: The Earth Summit opens in Rio de Janeiro
summary: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development gathered over 170 governments in Rio, where climate and biodiversity conventions were opened for signature.
reason: Growing concern over global warming, ozone depletion and deforestation called for a global response.
significance: It created the framework for later climate treaties, including Kyoto and Paris.

title: Rome Peace Accords end Mozambique's civil war
summary: The Mozambican government and the RENAMO rebels signed peace accords in Rome, mediated by the Community of Sant'Egidio.
reason: Sixteen years of war, famine and the end of Cold War backing left both sides exhausted.
significance: It ended a war that had killed about a million people and became a model for church-led mediation.

title: Babri Masjid is demolished in Ayodhya
summary: Hindu nationalist activists tore down the 16th-century mosque, claiming it stood on the birthplace of Rama. Riots across India killed about 2,000 people.
reason: A campaign by the VHP and BJP to build a Ram temple on the site had mobilised a vast crowd.
significance: It reshaped Indian politics and hardened Hindu-Muslim divisions.

title: Czechoslovakia splits into two states
summary: Czechoslovakia peacefully divided into the Czech Republic and Slovakia, without a referendum.
reason: Czech and Slovak leaders, Vaclav Klaus and Vladimir Meciar, could not agree on a shared constitution after 1989.
significance: It was a rare peaceful breakup of a state in post-communist Europe.

title: Oslo I Accord is signed at the White House
summary: Israel and the PLO signed a declaration of principles on Palestinian self-rule, sealed by a handshake between Yitzhak Rabin and Yasser Arafat.
reason: Secret talks in Norway after the first intifada and the Gulf War produced mutual recognition.
significance: It created the Palestinian Authority and framed peace efforts for decades.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Battle of Mogadishu
summary: US special forces raiding Mogadishu to capture aides of warlord Mohamed Farrah Aidid lost two Black Hawk helicopters, and 18 Americans and hundreds of Somalis died.
reason: The UN mission in Somalia had turned to hunting Aidid after his militia attacked peacekeepers.
significance: It made the US wary of intervening in Africa, which shaped its inaction in Rwanda.

title: NAFTA comes into force
summary: The North American Free Trade Agreement between Canada, Mexico and the United States took effect.
reason: Governments sought to boost trade and investment across North America by removing tariffs.
significance: It created one of the world's largest free trade areas.

title: The Rwandan genocide begins
summary: A day after the president's plane was shot down, Hutu extremists began killing Tutsi and moderate Hutu. About 800,000 people were murdered in 100 days.
reason: Decades of ethnic tension, civil war with the RPF and a prepared extremist network drove the killings.
significance: The world's failure to stop it reshaped thinking on humanitarian intervention.

title: Nelson Mandela becomes president of South Africa
summary: Nelson Mandela was sworn in as South Africa's first black president at the Union Buildings in Pretoria.
reason: The ANC won the country's first elections with universal suffrage in April 1994.
significance: It marked the formal end of apartheid.

title: Great Hanshin earthquake devastates Kobe
summary: A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck the Kobe area early in the morning, killing over 6,400 people.
reason: The fault ran directly under a dense port city with many older wooden houses.
significance: It exposed failures in Japan's disaster response and spurred a volunteer movement.

title: Sarin gas attack on the Tokyo subway
summary: Members of the Aum Shinrikyo cult released sarin on five subway trains, killing 13 people and harming thousands.
reason: The cult's leader Shoko Asahara preached an apocalypse and wanted to distract a coming police raid.
significance: It was the worst attack in postwar Japan and a landmark of chemical terrorism.

title: The Srebrenica massacre begins
summary: Bosnian Serb forces under Ratko Mladic overran the UN safe area of Srebrenica and over the following days killed about 8,000 Bosniak men and boys.
reason: Serb forces sought an ethnically pure territory, and Dutch peacekeepers were too few to resist.
significance: It was ruled a genocide and is the worst mass killing in Europe since 1945.

title: Amazon opens its online bookstore
summary: Jeff Bezos's Amazon.com began selling books online from a garage-born company in Seattle.
reason: Bezos saw that web use was exploding and that books suited mail-order selling from a huge catalogue.
significance: Amazon grew into one of the world's largest companies and reshaped retail.

title: First planet found orbiting a Sun-like star
summary: Michel Mayor and Didier Queloz announced 51 Pegasi b, a giant planet circling close to a Sun-like star.
reason: A new high-precision spectrograph let them detect the tiny wobble a planet causes in its star.
significance: It opened the field of exoplanets and earned a Nobel Prize in 2019.

title: Yitzhak Rabin is assassinated
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Yitzhak Rabin was shot dead by Yigal Amir after a peace rally in Tel Aviv.
reason: Amir, a right-wing extremist, opposed the Oslo Accords and handing land to the Palestinians.
significance: It dealt a lasting blow to the Israeli-Palestinian peace process.
place: Kings of Israel Square, Tel Aviv, Israel

title: Ken Saro-Wiwa is executed in Nigeria
summary: The Nigerian military regime hanged writer Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni activists after a widely condemned trial.
reason: Saro-Wiwa led a campaign against oil pollution by Shell and the government in the Niger Delta.
significance: It caused Nigeria's suspension from the Commonwealth and global outrage at oil industry abuses.
participants: Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People

title: Dayton Agreement ends the Bosnian War
summary: The leaders of Bosnia, Serbia and Croatia formally signed in Paris the peace deal negotiated in Dayton, Ohio.
reason: NATO bombing and Croatian and Bosniak offensives pushed the Bosnian Serbs to negotiate.
significance: It ended Europe's bloodiest war since 1945 and created Bosnia's current constitution.

title: Port Arthur massacre leads to gun reform in Australia
summary: A gunman killed 35 people at the Port Arthur historic site in Tasmania.
reason: The attacker had easy access to semi-automatic weapons.
significance: Within weeks Australia passed sweeping gun laws, a model cited around the world.

title: Dolly the sheep is born
summary: Dolly, the first mammal cloned from an adult cell, was born at the Roslin Institute in Scotland.
reason: Researchers sought ways to produce genetically modified livestock for medicine.
significance: It proved adult cells could be reprogrammed and launched debates on human cloning.

title: Nuclear Test-Ban Treaty opens for signature
summary: The Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty, banning all nuclear explosions, opened for signature at the UN, and Bill Clinton signed first.
reason: With the Cold War over, states sought to halt the development of new nuclear weapons.
significance: Though not in force, it has made nuclear testing almost unthinkable.
place: United Nations Headquarters, New York City, United States

title: Deep Blue defeats Garry Kasparov
summary: IBM's Deep Blue computer won the sixth game to beat world chess champion Garry Kasparov in a match.
reason: IBM had built specialised hardware to search millions of positions per second.
significance: It was the first match loss of a reigning world champion to a machine, a milestone for AI.

title: Britain hands Hong Kong to China
summary: At midnight Britain transferred sovereignty over Hong Kong to China, ending 156 years of British rule.
reason: The 1984 Sino-British Joint Declaration fixed the handover when the lease on the New Territories expired.
significance: It began the one country, two systems arrangement.
place: Hong Kong Convention and Exhibition Centre, Hong Kong

title: Thailand floats the baht, starting the Asian financial crisis
summary: Thailand gave up defending its currency's peg to the dollar, and the baht collapsed.
reason: Speculators attacked a currency backed by heavy foreign borrowing and a property bubble.
significance: The crisis spread across East Asia and toppled governments, including Suharto's.

title: Kyoto Protocol is adopted
summary: Delegates at a UN conference in Kyoto agreed binding cuts in greenhouse gas emissions for industrialised countries.
reason: Scientific evidence of global warming called for limits beyond the voluntary 1992 convention.
significance: It was the first legally binding climate treaty.
participants: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

title: Good Friday Agreement is signed
summary: The British and Irish governments and most Northern Irish parties agreed on power sharing in Belfast.
reason: After decades of the Troubles, ceasefires and mediation by George Mitchell made a settlement possible.
significance: It largely ended thirty years of conflict in Northern Ireland.

title: India carries out the Pokhran-II nuclear tests
summary: India exploded three nuclear devices at the Pokhran range, followed by two more two days later, and declared itself a nuclear state.
reason: India's new BJP government saw nuclear arms as a deterrent against China and Pakistan.
significance: It prompted Pakistan's tests and made South Asia openly nuclear.

title: Suharto resigns after 31 years
summary: Indonesian President Suharto stepped down amid mass protests and riots.
reason: The Asian financial crisis had wrecked Indonesia's economy and turned students and elites against him.
significance: It opened Indonesia's transition to democracy.

title: Al-Qaeda bombs US embassies in Kenya and Tanzania
summary: Truck bombs exploded almost simultaneously at the US embassies in Nairobi and Dar es Salaam, killing 224 people.
reason: Osama bin Laden's al-Qaeda had declared war on the United States over its troops in Saudi Arabia.
significance: It brought bin Laden to world attention and to the top of US target lists.

title: Google is incorporated
summary: Stanford students Larry Page and Sergey Brin incorporated Google, working from a garage in Menlo Park.
reason: Their PageRank algorithm ranked web pages by links and beat existing search engines.
significance: Google became the main gateway to information online.

title: Zarya, the first ISS module, is launched
summary: A Russian Proton rocket launched the Zarya module from Baikonur, beginning assembly of the International Space Station.
reason: Russia and the United States combined their space station plans after the Cold War.
significance: The ISS became the largest international science project in space.

title: Hugo Chavez wins Venezuela's presidency
summary: Former coup leader Hugo Chavez won the presidential election with about 56 percent of the vote.
reason: Voters were angry at corruption and poverty under the old two-party system.
significance: His Bolivarian revolution transformed Venezuela and influenced the Latin American left.

title: The euro is introduced
summary: Eleven European Union countries adopted the euro as their currency for banking and markets, with notes and coins following in 2002.
reason: The Maastricht Treaty set out monetary union to deepen the single market.
significance: It became the second most important reserve currency in the world.

title: NATO begins bombing Yugoslavia
summary: NATO launched air strikes against Yugoslavia over its crackdown in Kosovo, without UN Security Council approval.
reason: Serbian forces were expelling Kosovo Albanians, and talks at Rambouillet had failed.
significance: It was NATO's first war against a sovereign state and led to Kosovo's separation.

title: East Timor votes for independence
summary: In a UN-run referendum, 78.5 percent of East Timorese voted to leave Indonesia.
reason: After Suharto's fall, Indonesia allowed a vote on the territory it had occupied since 1975.
significance: Despite militia violence after the vote, it led to the independence of Timor-Leste in 2002.

title: Portugal hands Macau to China
summary: Portugal returned Macau to Chinese sovereignty after more than four centuries of Portuguese presence.
reason: A 1987 Sino-Portuguese declaration set the transfer under one country, two systems.
significance: It ended the last European colony in Asia.

title: First draft of the human genome is announced
summary: Bill Clinton and Tony Blair announced that the Human Genome Project and Celera Genomics had completed a working draft of the human genome.
reason: A public consortium and a private rival had raced to read all three billion DNA letters.
significance: It opened the era of genomic medicine.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Vicente Fox ends 71 years of PRI rule in Mexico
summary: Opposition candidate Vicente Fox of the PAN won Mexico's presidential election.
reason: Electoral reforms and public anger over corruption and economic crises weakened the ruling PRI.
significance: It completed Mexico's transition to multiparty democracy.

title: Second Intifada begins
summary: Ariel Sharon's visit to the Temple Mount sparked Palestinian protests that grew into a long uprising.
reason: The failure of the Camp David summit and frustration with occupation fuelled the anger.
significance: Years of violence killed thousands and buried the Oslo peace process.

title: First crew arrives at the International Space Station
summary: William Shepherd, Yuri Gidzenko and Sergei Krikalev docked with the ISS, starting continuous human presence in orbit.
reason: Enough modules were in place for a crew to live aboard.
significance: Humans have lived in space without a break ever since.
place: International Space Station, low Earth orbit

title: Wikipedia is launched
summary: Jimmy Wales and Larry Sanger launched Wikipedia, a free encyclopedia anyone could edit.
reason: It began as a wiki side project to speed up writing for the expert-written Nupedia.
significance: It became the largest reference work ever assembled.

title: September 11 attacks
summary: Al-Qaeda hijackers flew airliners into the World Trade Center and the Pentagon, and a fourth plane crashed in Pennsylvania. Nearly 3,000 people died.
reason: Osama bin Laden sought to punish the United States for its Middle East policies and provoke a wider war.
significance: It led to the war on terror, the invasions of Afghanistan and Iraq, and a new security era.
place: World Trade Center, New York City, United States

title: US-led invasion of Afghanistan begins
summary: The United States and Britain began bombing the Taliban and al-Qaeda, and Kabul fell within weeks.
reason: The Taliban refused to hand over Osama bin Laden after the September 11 attacks.
significance: It began a twenty-year war that ended with the Taliban's return in 2021.

title: China joins the World Trade Organization
summary: After fifteen years of negotiations, China formally became a member of the WTO.
reason: China's leaders wanted access to world markets to push reform and growth.
significance: It turned China into the world's factory and changed global trade.
wikipedia: China and the World Trade Organization

title: Argentina's economic crisis erupts in riots
summary: Looting and protests broke out across Argentina, and President Fernando de la Rua resigned the next day.
reason: A recession, a freeze on bank withdrawals and an unpayable debt under a dollar peg brought the economy to collapse.
significance: Argentina defaulted on its debt, then the largest sovereign default in history.
place: Plaza de Mayo, Buenos Aires, Argentina

title: Angola's civil war ends with a ceasefire
summary: Angola's government and UNITA signed a ceasefire memorandum in Luanda, six weeks after UNITA leader Jonas Savimbi was killed.
reason: Savimbi's death left the rebels leaderless and ready to negotiate.
significance: It ended a 27-year war that had killed hundreds of thousands.

title: The International Criminal Court is established
summary: The Rome Statute entered into force, creating a permanent court to try genocide, war crimes and crimes against humanity.
reason: The tribunals for Yugoslavia and Rwanda showed the need for a standing court.
significance: It became the first permanent international criminal court.

title: The African Union is launched
summary: The African Union replaced the Organisation of African Unity at a summit in Durban.
reason: African leaders wanted a stronger body to promote integration, peace and good governance.
significance: It became the continent's main political organisation.

title: Bali bombings kill 202
summary: Bombs exploded at nightclubs in Kuta, Bali, killing 202 people, many of them Australian tourists.
reason: The Islamist group Jemaah Islamiyah targeted Westerners in support of al-Qaeda's war.
significance: It was Indonesia's deadliest terror attack and brought the war on terror to Southeast Asia.

title: Space Shuttle Columbia breaks up on re-entry
summary: Columbia disintegrated over Texas while returning to Earth, killing all seven crew members.
reason: A piece of foam struck the wing at launch and damaged the heat shield.
significance: It led to the retirement of the shuttle fleet in 2011.

title: US-led invasion of Iraq begins
summary: American, British and allied forces began air strikes and a ground invasion of Iraq.
reason: The US accused Saddam Hussein of hiding weapons of mass destruction and links to terrorism, claims later shown false.
significance: It toppled Saddam but led to years of insurgency and sectarian war.

title: Yang Liwei becomes China's first astronaut
summary: China launched Shenzhou 5 with Yang Liwei aboard, who orbited Earth fourteen times.
reason: China had pursued crewed spaceflight since 1992 as a symbol of national power.
significance: China became the third country to send humans into space on its own.

title: Facebook is launched
summary: Mark Zuckerberg launched TheFacebook for Harvard students from his dormitory.
reason: Students wanted an online directory of classmates, and earlier campus sites had shown demand.
significance: It grew into the largest social network, reshaping media and politics.
place: Harvard University, Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States

title: European Union enlarges by ten countries
summary: Ten countries, mostly former communist states such as Poland, joined the European Union.
reason: After 1989 these states sought security, prosperity and a place in a united Europe.
significance: It was the largest single expansion of the EU and reunited the continent.

title: Orange Revolution begins in Ukraine
summary: Hundreds of thousands gathered in Kyiv's Independence Square to protest a rigged presidential runoff.
reason: Official results gave victory to Viktor Yanukovych despite widespread fraud against Viktor Yushchenko.
significance: A rerun election made Yushchenko president and showed Ukraine's turn toward the West.

title: Indian Ocean earthquake and tsunami
summary: A magnitude 9.1 earthquake off Sumatra sent tsunamis across the Indian Ocean, killing about 230,000 people in fourteen countries.
reason: The Indian Plate slipped under the Burma Plate along a 1,300 kilometre rupture, and there was no warning system in the ocean.
significance: It was one of the deadliest natural disasters in history and led to a global tsunami warning network.
place: Off the west coast of Sumatra, Indonesia

title: Rafic Hariri is assassinated in Beirut
summary: A huge truck bomb killed former Lebanese Prime Minister Rafic Hariri and 21 others in Beirut.
reason: Hariri had come to oppose Syria's military presence in Lebanon.
significance: Protests in the Cedar Revolution forced Syria to withdraw its troops.

title: Pope John Paul II dies
summary: Pope John Paul II died at the Vatican after nearly 27 years as pope. Millions came to Rome for his funeral.
reason: He had suffered from Parkinson's disease for years.
significance: His papacy had shaped the Catholic Church and the fall of communism in Poland.
wikipedia: Death and funeral of Pope John Paul II

title: First video is uploaded to YouTube
summary: YouTube co-founder Jawed Karim uploaded Me at the Zoo, an 18-second clip filmed at the San Diego Zoo.
reason: The founders wanted an easy way to share videos online.
significance: YouTube became the world's main video platform.
place: San Diego Zoo, California, United States

title: Hurricane Katrina hits the US Gulf Coast
summary: Katrina made landfall in Louisiana, and failing levees flooded most of New Orleans. About 1,400 people died.
reason: A strong storm met a city below sea level protected by poorly built levees.
significance: The slow response became a national scandal about poverty and government failure.

title: Earthquake kills over 80,000 in Kashmir
summary: A magnitude 7.6 earthquake struck near Muzaffarabad, devastating Pakistani Kashmir and northern Pakistan.
reason: The quake hit mountain villages with fragile buildings, and landslides cut off relief.
significance: It was the deadliest earthquake in South Asia's recent history.

title: North Korea conducts its first nuclear test
summary: North Korea set off an underground nuclear explosion at Punggye-ri.
reason: The regime sought nuclear weapons to guarantee its survival against the United States.
significance: It made North Korea a nuclear power and brought UN sanctions.

title: Steve Jobs unveils the iPhone
summary: At Macworld in San Francisco, Steve Jobs introduced the iPhone, a phone, iPod and internet device with a multi-touch screen.
reason: Apple wanted to enter the mobile market before phones replaced its iPod.
significance: It defined the smartphone and the app economy.
place: Moscone Center, San Francisco, United States

title: Benazir Bhutto is assassinated
summary: Former Pakistani Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto was killed by a gunman and suicide bomber after a rally in Rawalpindi.
reason: She had returned from exile to run in elections, defying threats from militants.
significance: Her death plunged Pakistan into unrest and hastened the end of Musharraf's rule.

title: Kosovo declares independence
summary: Kosovo's assembly declared independence from Serbia.
reason: UN administration since 1999 had failed to produce an agreed status.
significance: It is recognised by over a hundred states but not by Serbia, Russia or China.

title: Cyclone Nargis devastates Myanmar
summary: Cyclone Nargis struck the Irrawaddy Delta with a huge storm surge, killing about 138,000 people.
reason: The low delta was densely farmed, and the military junta gave little warning.
significance: The junta's blocking of foreign aid drew global condemnation.

title: Sichuan earthquake kills about 70,000
summary: A magnitude 7.9 earthquake struck Wenchuan county in Sichuan, collapsing towns and schools.
reason: The Longmenshan fault ruptured under mountainous, populated terrain.
significance: Collapsed schools sparked anger over shoddy construction in China.

title: Beijing Olympics open
summary: China opened the Games of the XXIX Olympiad with a spectacular ceremony at the Bird's Nest stadium.
reason: China sought to present itself as a modern world power.
significance: It marked China's arrival on the world stage.

title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
summary: The investment bank Lehman Brothers filed for the largest bankruptcy in US history, setting off a global panic.
reason: Lehman had huge losses on subprime mortgage securities, and the government refused to rescue it.
significance: It turned a credit crisis into the worst global recession since the 1930s.

title: Terrorists attack Mumbai
summary: Ten gunmen from Lashkar-e-Taiba arrived by sea and attacked hotels, a station and other sites in Mumbai over four days, killing 166 people.
reason: The Pakistan-based group sought to strike India and provoke conflict over Kashmir.
significance: It strained India-Pakistan relations and changed India's security policy.
place: Taj Mahal Palace Hotel, Mumbai, India

title: Bitcoin network starts with the genesis block
summary: The pseudonymous Satoshi Nakamoto mined the first block of the Bitcoin blockchain.
reason: Nakamoto wanted digital money without banks, a reaction to the financial crisis.
significance: It started cryptocurrencies and blockchain technology.

title: Barack Obama becomes US president
summary: Barack Obama was sworn in as the first African American president of the United States before a vast crowd in Washington.
reason: He won the 2008 election amid the financial crisis and fatigue with the Iraq war.
significance: It was a landmark for civil rights in the United States.
place: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Sri Lanka's civil war ends
summary: The Sri Lankan army defeated the Tamil Tigers in the northeast, and LTTE leader Velupillai Prabhakaran was killed.
reason: A massive offensive had cornered the rebels on a narrow coastal strip.
significance: It ended 26 years of war, though the final months killed tens of thousands of civilians.

title: Protests erupt over Iran's disputed election
summary: Huge crowds took to the streets of Tehran to protest the declared re-election of Mahmoud Ahmadinejad, forming the Green Movement.
reason: Supporters of Mir-Hossein Mousavi believed the vote had been rigged.
significance: They were the largest protests in Iran since 1979 and were violently crushed.

title: Earthquake devastates Haiti
summary: A magnitude 7.0 earthquake near Port-au-Prince killed between 100,000 and over 200,000 people.
reason: The fault lay near a crowded capital of poorly built concrete houses.
significance: It was one of the deadliest earthquakes ever and set back the poorest country in the Americas.

title: Deepwater Horizon oil rig explodes
summary: An explosion on BP's Deepwater Horizon rig killed eleven workers, and oil gushed into the Gulf of Mexico for 87 days.
reason: A failed cement seal and blowout preventer let gas rush up the well.
significance: It was the largest marine oil spill in history.
place: Gulf of Mexico, off Louisiana, United States

title: First football World Cup in Africa opens
summary: The FIFA World Cup opened at Soccer City in Johannesburg, the first held in Africa.
reason: South Africa won the bid as a symbol of its post-apartheid transformation.
significance: It brought the world's biggest sporting event to Africa for the first time.

title: Tunisian revolution begins
summary: Street vendor Mohamed Bouazizi set himself on fire in Sidi Bouzid, sparking protests that toppled President Ben Ali within a month.
reason: Unemployment, corruption and police abuse had built deep frustration.
significance: It ignited the Arab Spring across the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Egyptian revolution begins
summary: Protests began across Egypt, centred on Tahrir Square in Cairo, and forced Hosni Mubarak to resign on 11 February.
reason: Inspired by Tunisia, Egyptians rose against police brutality, poverty and 30 years of Mubarak's rule.
significance: It ended Mubarak's rule and became the centre of the Arab Spring.

title: Tohoku earthquake and tsunami strike Japan
summary: A magnitude 9.0 earthquake off northeastern Japan sent a tsunami that killed about 18,000 people and caused the Fukushima nuclear disaster.
reason: The Pacific Plate slipped violently under Japan along a huge section of fault.
significance: It was Japan's worst disaster since 1945 and turned many countries against nuclear power.
place: Off the Oshika Peninsula, Tohoku, Japan

title: Syrian uprising begins
summary: Protests calling for reform broke out in Damascus and soon in Daraa, and the government's violent response turned the uprising into civil war.
reason: The Arab Spring inspired Syrians angry at the Assad family's repressive rule.
significance: The war killed hundreds of thousands and created the largest refugee crisis of the century.

title: Osama bin Laden is killed
summary: US Navy SEALs raided a compound in Abbottabad, Pakistan, and killed al-Qaeda leader Osama bin Laden.
reason: US intelligence had traced him through a courier after nearly ten years of searching.
significance: It closed a chapter of the war on terror that began on 11 September 2001.

title: South Sudan becomes independent
summary: South Sudan declared independence from Sudan in Juba, becoming the world's newest country.
reason: Decades of civil war ended with a 2005 peace deal and a referendum in which almost all voters chose independence.
significance: It split Africa's largest country in two.

title: Muammar Gaddafi is killed
summary: Rebel fighters captured and killed Libya's former leader Muammar Gaddafi near Sirte.
reason: An uprising backed by NATO air strikes had driven him from power after 42 years.
significance: It ended his rule but left Libya divided and unstable.

title: CRISPR gene editing is shown to work
summary: Jennifer Doudna, Emmanuelle Charpentier and colleagues published the paper showing that CRISPR-Cas9 can be programmed to cut DNA at chosen sites.
reason: They had been studying how bacteria use CRISPR to defend against viruses.
significance: It made gene editing cheap and precise, and won the 2020 Nobel Prize.
place: University of California, Berkeley, United States

title: Discovery of the Higgs boson is announced
summary: CERN announced that the ATLAS and CMS experiments had found a new particle consistent with the Higgs boson.
reason: The Standard Model of physics predicted the particle in the 1960s, but it had never been seen.
significance: It confirmed how elementary particles get mass and earned Peter Higgs and Francois Englert the Nobel Prize.

title: Curiosity rover lands on Mars
summary: NASA's Curiosity rover was lowered onto Gale Crater by a rocket-powered sky crane.
reason: NASA wanted to know whether Mars ever had conditions able to support life.
significance: It found that ancient Mars had habitable lakes.

title: Delhi gang rape sparks nationwide protests
summary: A young woman was gang-raped on a bus in Delhi and died of her injuries, sparking mass protests across India.
reason: Anger had been growing over widespread sexual violence and police indifference.
significance: It led to tougher laws on sexual violence in India.

title: Jorge Mario Bergoglio is elected Pope Francis
summary: Cardinals elected the Argentine Jorge Mario Bergoglio, who took the name Francis.
reason: The conclave followed the first papal resignation in six centuries, by Benedict XVI.
significance: He was the first pope from the Americas and the first Jesuit pope.

title: Rana Plaza factory building collapses
summary: An eight-storey building housing garment factories collapsed in Savar near Dhaka, killing over 1,100 workers.
reason: Owners ignored cracks found the day before and ordered workers back inside.
significance: It was the deadliest garment industry disaster and forced global brands to sign safety accords.

title: Typhoon Haiyan strikes the Philippines
summary: One of the strongest tropical cyclones ever recorded at landfall hit the central Philippines, killing over 6,000 people, mostly in Tacloban.
reason: The storm surge swept across low coasts of Leyte and Samar.
significance: It became a symbol of climate vulnerability in poor countries.

title: Euromaidan protests begin in Kyiv
summary: Protests began in Kyiv after President Viktor Yanukovych suspended the signing of an association agreement with the EU.
reason: Many Ukrainians wanted closer ties to Europe and were angry at corruption.
significance: The protests toppled Yanukovych and led to Russia's seizure of Crimea.

title: Russia signs the annexation of Crimea
summary: Vladimir Putin signed a treaty in the Kremlin absorbing Crimea into Russia, two days after a disputed referendum.
reason: After the fall of Yanukovych, Russia seized the peninsula with soldiers without insignia.
significance: It was the first annexation of territory in Europe since 1945 and started the war in Ukraine.
wikipedia: Treaty on the Accession of the Republic of Crimea to Russia

title: Boko Haram kidnaps 276 schoolgirls in Chibok
summary: Boko Haram militants abducted 276 girls from a secondary school in Chibok, Nigeria.
reason: The Islamist group opposed Western education and used kidnapping as a weapon.
significance: The Bring Back Our Girls campaign drew world attention to the insurgency.

title: Islamic State captures Mosul
summary: Islamic State fighters seized Iraq's second largest city as the Iraqi army fled.
reason: The jihadist group exploited the Syrian war and Sunni anger at Iraq's government.
significance: Weeks later the group declared a caliphate, provoking a global coalition against it.

title: Earthquake devastates Nepal
summary: A magnitude 7.8 earthquake struck central Nepal, killing nearly 9,000 people and destroying historic temples in Kathmandu.
reason: The collision of the Indian and Eurasian plates builds up strain under the Himalayas.
significance: It was Nepal's worst disaster since 1934 and triggered a deadly avalanche on Everest.

title: US Supreme Court legalises same-sex marriage
summary: In Obergefell v. Hodges the Supreme Court ruled that same-sex couples have a constitutional right to marry.
reason: Plaintiffs challenged state bans after years of rapid change in public opinion.
significance: It made same-sex marriage legal in all fifty states.
participants: Supreme Court of the United States
place: Supreme Court Building, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Iran nuclear deal is agreed in Vienna
summary: Iran and six world powers agreed the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action, limiting Iran's nuclear program in return for lifting sanctions.
reason: Years of sanctions and fears of an Iranian bomb pushed both sides to negotiate.
significance: It was the biggest nuclear agreement in decades, though the US left it in 2018.

title: Gravitational waves are detected for the first time
summary: Both LIGO detectors in the United States recorded ripples in spacetime from two black holes merging over a billion years ago.
reason: Einstein predicted the waves in 1916, and decades of work had made detectors sensitive enough.
significance: It opened a new way of observing the universe and won the 2017 Nobel Prize.
place: LIGO Livingston Observatory, Louisiana, United States

title: Paris Agreement on climate change is adopted
summary: Nearly 200 countries agreed in Paris to keep global warming well below 2 degrees Celsius.
reason: Kyoto had failed to curb emissions, and leaders sought a deal that covered every country.
significance: It is the main global framework for fighting climate change.
participants: United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change

title: AlphaGo beats Go champion Lee Sedol
summary: DeepMind's AlphaGo won the first game of a five-game match in Seoul against Lee Sedol, one of the world's best Go players, and went on to win 4 to 1.
reason: Go was seen as too complex for computers, but deep learning let AlphaGo learn strong intuition.
significance: It showed the power of deep learning and began a new wave of AI.
place: Four Seasons Hotel, Seoul, South Korea

title: Panama Papers are published
summary: Journalists published reports based on 11.5 million leaked files from the law firm Mossack Fonseca, exposing offshore companies of politicians and the rich.
reason: An anonymous source leaked the files to a German newspaper, which shared them with a global network of reporters.
significance: It led to resignations, including Iceland's prime minister, and tougher rules on tax havens.

title: Britain votes to leave the European Union
summary: In a referendum, 51.9 percent of voters in the United Kingdom chose to leave the EU.
reason: David Cameron called the vote under pressure from Eurosceptics, amid concerns over immigration and sovereignty.
significance: Britain left the EU in 2020, the first country to do so.
wikipedia: 2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum

title: Coup attempt fails in Turkey
summary: A faction of the Turkish military tried to seize power, but crowds and loyal forces defeated it overnight. About 250 people died.
reason: The plotters opposed President Erdogan, who blamed the Gulen movement.
significance: Erdogan used it to purge tens of thousands and concentrate power.

title: Donald Trump wins the US presidential election
summary: Businessman Donald Trump defeated Hillary Clinton in the Electoral College despite losing the popular vote.
reason: He tapped anger over globalisation, immigration and the political establishment.
significance: His victory reshaped American politics and its relations with the world.

title: Colombia signs peace deal with the FARC
summary: President Juan Manuel Santos and FARC leader Rodrigo Londono signed a revised peace agreement in Bogota.
reason: After a first deal was rejected in a referendum, the two sides renegotiated to end a war of over fifty years.
significance: It ended the longest-running armed conflict in the Americas.

title: Military takes control in Zimbabwe, ending Mugabe's rule
summary: Zimbabwe's army seized control of Harare and placed President Robert Mugabe under house arrest. He resigned a week later.
reason: Mugabe had fired his deputy Emmerson Mnangagwa to clear the way for his wife Grace.
significance: It ended 37 years of rule by Mugabe.

title: Leaders of the two Koreas meet at Panmunjom
summary: Kim Jong Un stepped across the border to meet South Korea's Moon Jae-in, and they signed the Panmunjom Declaration.
reason: After a year of missile tests and threats, the 2018 Winter Olympics opened a diplomatic thaw.
significance: Kim was the first North Korean leader to enter South Korea.

title: Greta Thunberg starts her school strike for climate
summary: Fifteen-year-old Greta Thunberg began sitting outside the Swedish parliament instead of going to school.
reason: She wanted to press politicians to act on climate change after a summer of heat and wildfires.
significance: It grew into a global youth movement, Fridays for Future.

title: Chang'e 4 lands on the far side of the Moon
summary: China's Chang'e 4 probe made the first ever soft landing on the far side of the Moon and released the Yutu-2 rover.
reason: China had a step-by-step lunar program and used a relay satellite to talk to the hidden side.
significance: It showed China's rise as a leading space power.
place: Von Karman crater, far side of the Moon

title: Christchurch mosque shootings
summary: A white supremacist killed 51 people at two mosques in Christchurch, streaming the attack online.
reason: The attacker was driven by far-right conspiracy theories about immigration.
significance: New Zealand banned semi-automatic weapons and led a global effort against online extremism.
place: Al Noor Mosque, Christchurch, New Zealand

title: First image of a black hole is released
summary: The Event Horizon Telescope collaboration released an image of the shadow of the black hole at the centre of galaxy M87.
reason: Linking radio telescopes around the world created a virtual telescope the size of Earth.
significance: It gave the first direct visual evidence of a black hole.

title: India revokes Kashmir's special status
summary: India's government revoked the special autonomous status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370 and split the state in two.
reason: The BJP had long promised to integrate the Muslim-majority region fully into India.
significance: It was followed by a long communications blackout and raised tensions with Pakistan.
wikipedia: Revocation of the special status of Jammu and Kashmir

title: US drone strike kills Qasem Soleimani
summary: A US drone strike at Baghdad airport killed Iranian general Qasem Soleimani, head of the Quds Force.
reason: The US blamed him for attacks on American forces and an assault on its Baghdad embassy.
significance: It brought the US and Iran close to open war.

title: WHO declares COVID-19 a pandemic
summary: The World Health Organization declared the spread of the new coronavirus a pandemic.
reason: The virus, first identified in Wuhan, China, had spread to over 100 countries.
significance: The pandemic killed millions and brought lockdowns that changed life worldwide.

title: George Floyd is murdered by police in Minneapolis
summary: George Floyd died after officer Derek Chauvin knelt on his neck for over nine minutes, setting off protests worldwide.
reason: A bystander's video revealed the killing, adding to long anger over police violence against Black Americans.
significance: It led to the largest protest movement in US history.

title: SpaceX launches its first astronauts
summary: SpaceX's Crew Dragon carried NASA astronauts Bob Behnken and Doug Hurley to the International Space Station.
reason: Since the shuttle's retirement, NASA had relied on Russia and paid private firms to build spacecraft.
significance: It was the first crewed orbital flight by a private company.
place: Kennedy Space Center, Florida, United States

title: Massive explosion devastates Beirut
summary: Ammonium nitrate stored in Beirut's port exploded, killing over 200 people and wrecking much of the city.
reason: About 2,750 tonnes of the chemical had been left unsafely in a warehouse for six years.
significance: It became a symbol of corruption and state failure in Lebanon.

title: Abraham Accords are signed
summary: Israel, the United Arab Emirates and Bahrain signed agreements at the White House to normalise relations.
reason: Shared hostility to Iran and US mediation brought the Gulf states and Israel together.
significance: They were the first Arab-Israeli normalisation deals since 1994.
place: White House, Washington, D.C., United States

title: AlphaFold solves protein structure prediction
summary: The organisers of the CASP14 competition announced that DeepMind's AlphaFold predicted protein structures almost as accurately as experiments.
reason: Predicting a protein's shape from its amino acids had been a 50-year challenge in biology.
significance: It transformed biology and won the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry.

title: First approved COVID-19 vaccine dose is given
summary: Margaret Keenan, aged 90, received the Pfizer-BioNTech vaccine in Coventry, the first person given an approved COVID-19 vaccine outside a trial.
reason: mRNA technology let vaccines be developed in under a year.
significance: Mass vaccination saved millions of lives.
place: University Hospital Coventry, England, United Kingdom

title: Supporters of Donald Trump storm the US Capitol
summary: A mob attacked the US Capitol to stop Congress from certifying Joe Biden's election victory.
reason: Trump had falsely claimed the 2020 election was stolen and urged his supporters to march on the Capitol.
significance: It was the first violent disruption of a US transfer of power.
place: United States Capitol, Washington, D.C., United States

title: Military coup in Myanmar
summary: Myanmar's military detained Aung San Suu Kyi and other leaders and seized power.
reason: The army rejected the landslide election win of Suu Kyi's party, claiming fraud.
significance: It ended a decade of partial democracy and led to civil war.

title: The Taliban take Kabul
summary: Taliban fighters entered Kabul as President Ashraf Ghani fled, completing their takeover of Afghanistan.
reason: The US had agreed to withdraw its troops, and the Afghan army collapsed in weeks.
significance: It ended twenty years of the Western-backed republic.

title: James Webb Space Telescope is launched
summary: An Ariane 5 rocket launched the James Webb Space Telescope from French Guiana.
reason: Astronomers wanted an infrared telescope to see the first galaxies and study exoplanet atmospheres.
significance: It is the most powerful space telescope ever built.
place: Guiana Space Centre, Kourou, French Guiana

title: Russia launches full-scale invasion of Ukraine
summary: Russian forces attacked Ukraine from the north, east and south, including an advance on Kyiv.
reason: Vladimir Putin denied Ukraine's right to exist as a sovereign state and opposed its turn to the West.
significance: It is the largest war in Europe since 1945.

title: Queen Elizabeth II dies
summary: Queen Elizabeth II died at Balmoral Castle aged 96, after 70 years on the throne, and Charles III became king.
reason: She had been in frail health for months.
significance: She was the longest-reigning British monarch.
wikipedia: Death and state funeral of Elizabeth II

title: Death of Mahsa Amini sparks protests in Iran
summary: Mahsa Amini, 22, died in custody after her arrest by Iran's morality police for improper hijab, sparking nationwide protests.
reason: Iranians, led by women, were angry at compulsory veiling and repression.
significance: The Woman, Life, Freedom movement became the largest challenge to the Islamic Republic in years.

title: ChatGPT is released
summary: OpenAI released ChatGPT, a chatbot built on a large language model, which gained 100 million users within two months.
reason: Advances in large language models made fluent conversation possible.
significance: It started a global boom in generative AI.

title: Argentina wins the World Cup in Qatar
summary: Argentina beat France on penalties after a 3 to 3 draw in Lusail, with Lionel Messi named player of the tournament.
reason: Qatar hosted the first World Cup in the Arab world.
significance: The final is often called the greatest in World Cup history.

title: Chandrayaan-3 lands near the Moon's south pole
summary: India's Chandrayaan-3 lander touched down near the lunar south pole.
reason: India sought to succeed after its 2019 lander crashed and to study ice near the pole.
significance: India became the fourth country to soft-land on the Moon and the first near its south pole.

title: Hamas attacks Israel
summary: Hamas-led militants broke out of Gaza and killed about 1,200 people in Israel and took over 250 hostages.
reason: Hamas sought to strike Israel and derail Saudi-Israeli normalisation, amid a long blockade of Gaza.
significance: It started the Gaza war, which killed tens of thousands and spread conflict across the region.

title: Sheikh Hasina resigns and flees Bangladesh
summary: Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina resigned and fled to India as protesters marched on her residence in Dhaka.
reason: Student protests over job quotas turned into a mass uprising after hundreds were killed.
significance: It ended fifteen years of her rule and led to an interim government under Muhammad Yunus.

title: Assad regime falls in Syria
summary: Rebels led by Hayat Tahrir al-Sham entered Damascus as Bashar al-Assad fled to Moscow.
reason: A lightning offensive met an army hollowed out by years of war, while Assad's allies Russia, Iran and Hezbollah were weakened.
significance: It ended more than fifty years of rule by the Assad family.

title: Powerful earthquake strikes central Myanmar
summary: A magnitude 7.7 earthquake on the Sagaing Fault struck near Mandalay, killing thousands in Myanmar and toppling a tower in Bangkok.
reason: The Sagaing Fault ruptured over hundreds of kilometres in a shallow quake.
significance: It was Myanmar's strongest quake in over a century, made worse by the civil war.

title: Robert Prevost is elected Pope Leo XIV
summary: Cardinals elected Robert Francis Prevost, who took the name Leo XIV, after the death of Pope Francis.
reason: The conclave sought a successor able to continue Francis's reforms and unite the church.
significance: He is the first pope from the United States.
